body.statement: Determine \(M^{\star}\), the smallest universal worst-case number of distinct channel evaluations required to recover one sharp endpoint over all nonempty feasible polygons in this model. Establish both a reduction from the ten-point map and a realizable configuration proving that no smaller cap suffices, while preserving endpoint attainment in the strict model.
body.justification: The proved constant-size map need not be combinatorially minimal, and minimality is the honest open mathematical content beyond completeness.
body.gap: No cited benefit-bound or misclassification paper studies the worst-case evaluation complexity of a shared-channel semialgebraic envelope.
body.consumer: A sharp cap yields the smallest auditable branch set for exact arithmetic and formal verification.

obligation.what_is_open: A matching lower bound for \(M^{\star}\), and therefore the exact minimal universal cap, remains open.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen handle does not define the admissible algorithm or information model behind a required channel evaluation. A configuration with ten distinct candidate incidences does not imply that all ten objective values must be queried, because algebraic dominance tests may discard candidates without evaluation. Thus a no-smaller-cap claim is not well typed from the present primitives.
obligation.attempted: The boundary arrangement was reduced to at most five vertices, four stationary-line contacts, and one informativeness-edge contact. Realizable incidence patterns can make all ten locations distinct, but that only lower-bounds the cardinality of the unpruned candidate set, not the query complexity of every exact endpoint procedure.
obligation.partial_result:
The finite-envelope proof establishes the computable upper bound \(M^{\star}\leq10\) for direct evaluation of the declared candidate map, and \(M^{\star}\leq8\) when the informativeness cut is absent.  Ten distinct candidate incidences are realizable.  For example, take
\[
 [u_L,u_U]=[0,2/5],\quad [v_L,v_U]=[1/2,1],\quad
 \kappa=3/10,\quad (q_0,q_1)=(21/50,12/25),\quad \theta=16.
\]
Then \(D\) is the pentagon with vertices
\[
 (0,1/2),(1/5,1/2),(2/5,7/10),(2/5,1),(0,1).
\]
The stationary sums are \(33/50\) and \(57/50\), giving the four distinct axis-edge contacts
\[
 (0,33/50),(4/25,1/2),(2/5,37/50),(7/50,1),
\]
while the central informativeness-edge contact is \((3/10,3/5)\).  None coincides with a vertex, and the whole polygon is strictly compatible because \(u\leq2/5<21/50\) and \(v\geq1/2>12/25\).  This realizes ten candidate locations while preserving strict compatibility.  It still does not prove that every exact endpoint algorithm must evaluate all ten: incidence cardinality is not an information-based query lower bound, and algebraic dominance tests may discard locations without evaluating the root there.
